images.title: Counting eighths on a strip
images.purpose: Show that a 1 unit strip in 8 equal parts has the unit 1/8, that 3 parts are 3 × 1/8 = 3/8, and that 8 parts are the whole strip.
images.composition: Two strips of exactly the same length stacked with wide space between: the eighths strip on top and a plain whole strip below for comparison.
images.exact_structure: Top: one strip, 1 unit long, split by 7 grey #6B7280 creases into 8 exactly equal parts; the first 3 parts from the left filled teal #0072B2, the other 5 plain; a reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket above the 3 teal parts; the leftmost part carries a small label. Below: one strip of exactly the same length, filled amber #E69F00, not divided. Exactly 2 strips, 8 equal parts, 1 bracket.

images.takeaway: Count the parts on top and keep the unit eighths: 3 parts are 3/8.
images.description: A 1 unit strip in 8 equal parts with the first 3 shaded and bracketed as 3 × 1/8 = 3/8, above a same-length whole strip marked 8 × 1/8 = 1 whole.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the bracketed parts and say the length as a number of eighths.

image_decisions.why: A strip in eighths above the whole strip shows lengths counted in the unit one eighth up to one whole.
